statements.t: • Reduced net debt (1) by over $500 million through the end of the third quarter and are on track to achieve our 20% debt reduction target in 2026

Looking ahead, our focus remains clear and we expect to make continued progress against our four strategic priorities, entering 2027 in a much stronger position with multiple catalysts across the portfolio to create additional value.”

With strong operational performance for the year and continued debt reduction, we are on track to achieve our ~20% net debt reduction target for 2026 with year-end net debt expected to be below $2.4 billion and leverage expected to fall towards 2.0x.

Production in the Gulf of America averaged approximately 14,100 boepd net (~83% oil) during the third quarter, in line with guidance, reflecting continued strong performance from the Company's operated assets, partially offset by host facility downtime.

In the fourth quarter, Gulf of America production is expected to be impacted by planned Delta House platform maintenance (Odd Job host facility), a workover on the Kodiak-1 well and downtime associated with Hurricane Isaias, and has been reflected in the Company's fourth quarter guidance.
We achieved a final investment decision in March 2026 with first oil targeted in the second half of 2028.

In July 2026, Kosmos and Occidental completed a farm-down transaction with Navitas Petroleum US, LLC, resulting in Navitas acquiring a 33.33% interest in the project alongside Kosmos (33.34%) and Occidental (33.33%), an owner and operator of the host facility.
The Company maintains insurance coverage that it expects will offset a significant portion of any remediation costs that may be incurred to restore the Winterfell-2 well to normal operations.
We are actively engaged in an ongoing process of anticipating and meeting our funding requirements related to our strategy as a deepwater exploration and production company.
Our investment decisions are based on longer-term commodity prices based on the nature of our projects and development plans.
Current commodity prices, combined with our hedging program and our current liquidity position is expected to support our remaining capital program for 2026.
For our capital expenditure budget for the last quarter of 2026, we expect to incur capital costs as we advance development efforts in Ghana, the Gulf of America and in Mauritania and Senegal.

These include the number of wells we plan to drill, our paying interests in our operations including disproportionate payment amounts, the costs involved in developing or participating in the development of a prospect, the timing of third‑party projects, the availability of suitable equipment and qualified personnel and our cash flows from operations.

We may need to raise additional funds more quickly if market conditions deteriorate, or one or more of our assumptions proves to be incorrect, or if we choose to expand our acquisition, exploration, appraisal, development efforts or any other activity more rapidly than we presently anticipate.
We estimate we will spend in aggregate around $350 million of capital for the year ending December 31, 2026, excluding any acquisitions or divestitures of oil and gas properties during the year.
The ultimate amount of capital we will spend may fluctuate materially based on market conditions and the success of our exploitation and drilling results among other factors.
Based on our monitoring activities, we currently believe our banks will be able to perform on their commitments.

The Capped Call Transactions are generally expected to reduce potential dilution to holders of our common stock upon any conversion of the 3.125% Convertible Senior Notes and/or offset any cash payments that we are required to make in excess of the principal amount of any 3.125% Convertible Senior Notes that are converted, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap.
